questions.q: Why does this lesson say environment strategy is architecture work, not just operational housekeeping?
options: Because sandboxes are irrelevant to real production risk
Because a poorly designed environment strategy causes real, expensive defects and delays, the same category of damage a bad data model or sharing model causes
Because environment strategy has no connection to a technical architect's role
Because Salesforce automatically manages environment strategy with no human input needed
questions.explain: Deciding how changes move safely from idea to production is part of an architect's accountability for a solution's long-term integrity — a bad environment strategy (e.g., building against something too close to production) causes real, costly problems.

questions.q: Which sandbox type copies metadata only and is meant for one developer's (or a small team's) day-to-day feature coding?
options: Full sandbox
Partial Copy sandbox
Developer sandbox
Production org
questions.explain: The Developer sandbox copies metadata only, with limited storage and a short refresh cycle, making it the right fit for everyday individual or small-team feature coding and unit testing.

questions.q: What is a Partial Copy sandbox typically used for?
options: Final pre-release staging at full production scale
Integration testing and user acceptance testing, using metadata plus a configured sample of production data
Permanent production hosting
Disposable, source-defined feature work with no copied data at all
questions.explain: A Partial Copy sandbox copies metadata plus a configured sample of production data via a sandbox template, giving testers realistic-enough data for integration and UAT testing without needing the full production dataset.

questions.q: How does a scratch org differ conceptually from a traditional sandbox?
options: A scratch org is just another name for a Full sandbox
A scratch org isn't a sandbox at all — it's a disposable, fully configurable environment typically rebuilt from source-controlled configuration rather than copied from production
A scratch org always contains a full copy of production data
A scratch org cannot be used in any automated pipeline
questions.explain: Unlike sandboxes, which are copied/refreshed from production, a scratch org is defined and rebuilt from source-controlled configuration, commonly used for short-lived feature work in DX-based development pipelines.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what matters more than which specific tool (change sets, managed package, CI/CD) is used to move changes to production?
options: Using the single most expensive tool available
Whether the deployment path is actually documented, consistent, and followed every time, rather than skipped under deadline pressure
Whether the change set is approved by the CEO personally
Avoiding version control entirely to move faster
questions.explain: The specific tool matters less than whether the path is consistently followed. A one-off change pushed directly to production outside the normal pipeline, skipped under deadline pressure, is a common real cause of production incidents a proper process would have caught.
